about.title: Newark Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Newark's mix of industrial parks, warehouses, and commercial corridors near Cherry Street and Newark Boulevard means workplace accidents happen more often than most people expect. In California, workers' compensation is typically the only path against your employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. Alameda County workers navigating these overlapping systems often benefit from talking to someone who can sort out which rules apply to their situation. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees; we simply connect injured Newark workers with an independent attorney who can review the facts and explain what's realistic. Whether your injury happened operating machinery, driving for work, or on a job site shared with outside contractors, understanding your full range of options matters before you sign anything or accept a settlement.

whyChoose.title: Why Newark Workers Consider Legal Help

items.title: Third-Party Claims Exist Alongside Workers' Comp
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually exclusive against your employer, a separate claim against a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may be your only route to full compensation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early
items.desc: California requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, so getting guidance quickly helps protect both your comp benefits and any potential third-party claim.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Are in Place
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: I already filed a workers' comp claim in Newark. Can I still pursue something else?
items.answer: Yes, workers' comp and a third-party claim are separate legal tracks. If someone other than your employer, like a subcontractor or equipment supplier, contributed to your injury, you may still have a claim against them even while receiving comp benefits.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim in California?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. Workers' comp reporting timelines are shorter, so it helps to get informed early rather than waiting.

items.question: Does it matter that my injury happened near a busy Newark corridor like Thornton Avenue?
items.answer: It can. If your injury involved a work vehicle collision on roads like Thornton Avenue or Cedar Boulevard, another driver's negligence could support a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. An attorney can help determine whether that applies to your case.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No, California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report injuries or file workers' comp claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can advise you on next steps.
